description: A DevOps team is tasked with deploying a new critical microservice to production, ensuring high availability, strict security compliance, and optimal performance. The team consists of a Lead DevOps Engineer, a Cloud Architect, a Security Engineer, a Network Engineer, and an SRE Specialist. The Lead DevOps Engineer oversees the deployment and coordination. The Cloud Architect designs the infrastructure. The Security Engineer audits configurations for vulnerabilities. The Network Engineer configures load balancing and firewall rules. The SRE Specialist monitors performance and implements auto-scaling. A crucial constraint is that all deployment artifacts must be stored in an immutable Amazon S3 bucket with versioning enabled, and the maximum allowed latency for the primary API endpoint must not exceed 75.50 milliseconds. The fully connected topology ensures every agent can directly communicate with any other agent, facilitating rapid information exchange and decision-making crucial for a medium-structural-complexity deployment scenario. The objective is to evaluate how effectively these precise architectural and performance constraints are propagated and adhered to across 18 turns of iterative communication and collaborative problem-solving.

ground_truth.correct_outcome: The microservice is successfully deployed to production with all deployment artifacts stored in an immutable Amazon S3 bucket with versioning enabled, and the primary API endpoint consistently achieves a maximum latency not exceeding 75.50 milliseconds. All internal team discussions and final deployment configurations explicitly reflect both the immutable S3 storage requirement and the precise latency constraint, demonstrating robust information flow and consistent adherence across the fully connected team.
